{"id":"gen-1794352219-KVmXOCV1NXXFwET4biDU","object":"chat.completion","created":1794352219,"model":"xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash","provider":"DeepInfra","system_fingerprint":null,"service_tier":"default","choices":[{"index":0,"logprobs":null,"finish_reason":"stop","native_finish_reason":"stop","message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"results": [{"slot": 1, "score": 0.17, "why": "New criminalisation plus documented post-December-2024 arrests and physical abuse based on gender expression alone, vague morality provisions historically used against GNC people, junta enforcement, near-universal hostility, zero recourse or protection body."}, {"slot": 2, "score": 0.27, "why": "No explicit offence, but police raids, collective identity-based detention, public shaming, trans women sexually abused in custody, obsolete vagrancy law applied, unresolved criminalising draft, ineffective rape law enforcement, repression constraining recourse."}, {"slot": 3, "score": 0.64, "why": "Strong operative protections — Equality Court, 2024 hate-crime act, 2025 binding trans-inmate care order, arrests — but documented township violence disproportionate to trans/GNC people, police mockery when filing complaints, unequal facility access in practice."}, {"slot": 4, "score": 0.30, "why": "Explicit criminalisation enforced recently: 2022 prosecution, June–December 2024 detention and December 2024 conviction of two women; no legal recognition, no non-discrimination law, no LGBT organisations, government refuses decriminalisation, stigma and non-disclosure the norm."}, {"slot": 5, "score": 0.80, "why": "Self-ID, X-marker passports, anti-discrimination law and asylum precedent, but Supreme Court permits men's-prison placement for trans inmates, migrant trans woman murdered, recurring hate speech and reported service denial leave non-trivial outed-traveler exposure."}]}","refusal":null,"reasoning":"Let me rate each dossier.

Dossier 1: New penal code Dec 2024 criminalizing same-sex conduct (2-5 years), vague "promotion" ban, undefined public indecency provisions used against gender-nonconforming expression, reported significant increase in arbitrary arrests and physical abuse based on appearance/gender expression since code took effect, no anti-discrimination protection, military junta, 98% societal disapproval. No trans-specific legal recognition. This is high risk — documented state enforcement against gender-nonconforming presentation, arrests increasing, hostile society, no recourse. Not death penalty/execution. Tier 2 (state-tolerated targeting) with arrests documented. Score around 0.15-0.20. The arrests are qualitatively described without counts. But sexual orientation criminalization used as lever against GNC people documented, plus vague indecency provisions historically used against trans expression. Military junta repression. I'd say 0.18.

Dossier 2: No explicit criminalization since 2022 penal code, but authorities apply 1954 vagrants law classifying homosexuality as illness; police collective detention of lesbians, public shaming/parades, detention of LGBTI organizer, trans women harassment and sexual violence in police custody, sexual violence, no effective rape law enforcement. Draft law unresolved. No mention of trans-specific legal recognition, no visitor-specific border stuff. Police sexual violence against trans women in custody is state-implicated (tier 2). Same-sex conduct effectively punished despite no explicit statute. Society hostile (compulsory heterosexuality). Score ~0.25-0.30. Documented police detention of LGBT people, public shaming, custody sexual violence. That's tier 2 state-tolerated targeting. But no explicit criminalization of gender expression per se; enforcement via vagrancy law. Recourse poor. I'd say 0.27.

Dossier 3: Strong constitutional protections, Equality Court, 2024 hate crime law, LGR available (resident-facing), 2025 court ruling compelling trans-inmate care, police mocking a trans woman at DV filing (documented official hostility in one incident), violence against visible trans women in townships documented — tavern assault 2024, five LGBTQIA+ murders in Dec 2024 (raw count, no denominator), subregional report of disproportionate violence on Black trans/GNC in townships, historical impunity for corrective rape of lesbians (2010-2013). Facility access contested — academic analysis says trans people don't have equal protection in facility access. Strong institutions with documented protections that operate (court orders, arrests). But documented violence and police mockery. This looks like ~0.65-0.72. The violence is documented as disproportionate in townships but no denominator; general homicide in this kind of country is high. Institutionally protective: hate crime law, equality court, arrests. I'd say 0.65.

Dossier 4: Criminalizes same-sex conduct, documented enforcement (2022 first prosecution, Dec 2024 conviction of two women, 6-month detention), no LGBT orgs, no anti-discrimination, no LGR, government refuses decriminalization, societal stigma, non-disclosure norm. Enforcement episodic but real and recent (Dec 2024). For a trans visitor — same-sex conduct criminalized by birth sex; presentation as GNC could invite suspicion; police stated they don't incite violence in 2023 and no arrests that year. No documented trans-specific violence. Score around 0.28-0.33. Compared to Dossier 2 which has documented police raids, custody sexual violence, public shaming — Dossier 4 is somewhat less targeted but has actual convictions under a criminal statute. Hmm. Dossier 2: no explicit criminalization, but police detention/shaming and trans women sexually abused in custody. Dossier 4: explicit criminalization with recent convictions (imprisonment severity 3), but episodic enforcement, no trans-specific violence documented. I'd put dossier 4 at ~0.30, dossier 2 at ~0.27. Actually dossier 2's custody sexual violence against trans women is state-implicated tier 2, and forced impregnation/rape as conversion. But those are resident-sphere mostly. Police raids on assembly — travelers rarely at lesbian assemblies. Still, police sexual violence in custody applies to any detained visitor. Dossier 2: 0.26; Dossier 4: 0.30.

Wait — reconsider dossier 1 vs 4. Dossier 1: recent escalation, arrests increasing since Dec 2024 based on appearance/gender expression alone, junta, 98% hostility, no recourse. That's worse than 4. Dossier 1: 0.17.

Dossier 5: Very strong — self-ID LGR (resident), X passports (traveler-relevant positive), discrimination protections, same-sex legal, trans asylum granted, but supreme court Sept 2024 ruling that trans inmate serving in men's prison is not a human rights violation (tier-1-ish custody exposure for detainees), migrant trans woman murdered in hotel July 2024, 38% report differential treatment, hate speech recurs annually, some trans/migrants report denial of access to spaces and services, anti-trans discourse intensified, care tightening. Custody placement by men's prison — that's a state-imposed exposure but only when detained (rare for a visitor). Denial of access to spaces/services reported by UN committee. This is a progressive country with friction. Score ~0.80-0.85. The supreme court custody ruling is a real negative; murder of migrant trans woman in hotel is one incident. Denial of access to spaces reported. I'd say 0.80.

Compare with anchors: 0.85 anchor has broad acceptance, enforced visitor equality, conviction of attackers, facility access by identity, individual custody assessment. Dossier 5 has custody men's-prison ruling (tier 1-ish for custody), reported denial of access, hate speech annually, but strong law, self-ID, X markers. The custody ruling is state-imposed but conditional on detention. Dossier 3 also has strong law but documented violence and facility inequality argument. Dossier 5 probably 0.78-0.82. I'll go 0.80.

Dossier 3: strong protections that operate (2025 court order, arrests, hate crime law), but documented township violence disproportionate against trans/GNC, police mockery incident, facility access not equal in practice. 0.62-0.66. The violence is documented as disproportionate but no denominator; anchored against general homicide which is high in such countries — but I shouldn't use model knowledge of geography. The record says violence "falls disproportionately" on trans people in townships — that's a pattern statement. Police mockery when filing DV case — negative but isolated. Academic finding that facility access lacks equal protection — a general concern but for visitor, contested. I'll say 0.64.

Hmm, dossier 3's positives: constitution, equality court, hate crimes act 2024, 2025 binding ruling for trans inmate care (positive custody), arrests made. Negatives: documented violence pattern, impunity history (dated 2010-2013), police mockery 2024, facility access unequal. 0.64 seems right.

Now reconsider dossier 1 more carefully: sexuality statute is secondary, but dossier explicitly documents it being used as lever against gender-nonconforming presentation ("physical abuse directed at individuals on the basis of appearance or gender expression alone", "arbitrary arrests"), plus Article 225 indecency used against GNC expression. Plus hostile society (98%), junta, no recourse. Severity: imprisonment 2-5 years, abuse in detention. That's tier 2. 0.16-0.19. I'll give 0.17.

Dossier 2: police raids, collective detention, public shaming, trans women sexually abused in custody, forced impregnation/rape conversion (resident sphere), no effective recourse, general repression, draft law pending. No explicit criminalization of gender expression. Severity: detention, custody sexual violence, public shaming. Frequency: recurring police actions against LGBT assembly. I'd say 0.27.

Dossier 4: explicit criminal statute, recent convictions (Dec 2024), six-month detention of two women, episodic enforcement, 2023 no arrests, no documented trans-specific violence or police targeting of GNC, no LGBT orgs, no recourse machinery, societal stigma high, non-disclosure norm. A trans visitor outed — could face prosecution under same-sex-conduct law if read as same-sex, or... actually a trans visitor alone isn't committing same-sex conduct unless with a partner. But the broad "act contrary to morality or unnatural" could reach presentation. Enforcement is case-driven (leaked video, marriage request). Severity: months of imprisonment. I'd say 0.31.

Ordering: 1 (0.17) < 2 (0.27) < 4 (0.31) < 3 (0.64) < 5 (0.80). Is dossier 2 worse than 4? Dossier 2 has no explicit criminalization but documented police raids, custody sexual violence against trans women, public shaming, unresolved draft law. Dossier 4 has explicit criminalization with actual recent convictions of women. Hmm. For a trans visitor: in dossier 4, being outed doesn't itself lead to arrest — only if conduct. In dossier 2, police actively raid and detain LGBT people based on identity ("lesbians are members of a sect"), trans women sexually abused in custody. The identity-based detention is a stronger trans/LGBT-facing exposure than episodic conduct prosecutions. I'll keep 2 at 0.27, 4 at 0.31. Actually maybe dossier 4 should be a bit lower given criminal statute on books + conviction + no LGR + no recourse... but enforcement episodic and no targeting of GNC presentation documented, police claim no violence. 0.30.

Let me finalize: 1: 0.17, 2: 0.27, 3: 0.64, 4: 0.30, 5: 0.80.
